change_summary: Select the processing profile before source-body enumeration so the Host preserves exact inputs, gives Corvio a weak Asset-handle handoff, and waits for terminal Work Model readback without precomputing taxonomy or opening duplicate operations.

canonical_skill.note: The Workspace Skill resolves the remaining semantic bottleneck before reading source bodies, forbids Host-side corpus enumeration as a downgrade signal, keeps source facts behind Asset handles, and moves the terminal-operation boundary into the first decision table.

server_contract.note: The server advertises Skill release 1.7.67 and collaboration contract 2026-09-17.6 while retaining Mission branch-level source sufficiency as the semantic organization owner.

package_manifests.note: Skill and Plugin manifests advance together to 1.7.67; compatibility family and minimum revision remain unchanged.

workspace_cli.note: Workspace and Admin CLI remain at 0.1.0-beta.35; their shared server-discovered processing-profile contract remains compatible and needs no CLI protocol change.

help_center.note: Public Help remains compatible because the public Skill page projects this shared package and the release does not change remote MCP connection or installation steps.

package_setup.note: SessionStart reports Skill 1.7.67 and foregrounds bounded preflight, no Host-side corpus enumeration, and profile selection before source-body interpretation.

harness_and_mainline.note: The Harness keeps selected-Workspace routing and adds released-host evidence that source enumeration belongs behind Corvio Asset handles rather than in the Host prompt.

external_marketplaces.note: First-party publication, public hashes and fresh released-host readback remain release gates; external directory acceptance stays outside repository authority.

release_evidence.note: Backend, Skill, external-host, and frontend package-contract tests assert the new release, pre-enumeration profile boundary, weak handoff, terminal completion, selected-Workspace receipt, and source-coverage sufficiency rule.
